title: Potere, volere, dovere
summary: The modal verbs potere, volere, dovere + infinitive — Italian's politeness engine.

blocks.title: I tre modali
blocks.body: Three verbs do enormous work in Italian: **potere** (can/may — permission, ability), **volere** (want), and **dovere** (must/have to). Each pairs with a plain **infinitive**: *posso entrare?* (can I come in?), *voglio provare* (I want to try), *devo andare* (I have to go). This modal + infinitive pattern is the engine behind almost every polite request.
blocks.callout: Same three endings (-o / -i / -e) as every other verb you've drilled — just irregular stems.

pairs.note: Same verb 'uscire' (to go out), totally different meaning depending on the modal.

blocks.explain: *Dovere* — obligation. *Devo studiare* = I have to study, whether I like it or not.

blocks.prompt: Type 'Can I have a coffee?' using potere.
blocks.explain: *Posso avere un caffè?* — polite, and works everywhere from a bar to a friend's kitchen.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type the whole line.

lines.en: I have to go back to work.
